runtime.subscription: claude.ai login; cost_usd in receipts is API-equivalent, not a bill
runtime.baseline_before_v1: every subagent inherited the main model (claude-fable-5-1) at effort xhigh (settings.json effortLevel)

find_feature.what: locate code, callers, fields, dispatch targets in a huge codebase with search tools; no writes
find_feature.why_no_escalation: misses are confident answers, there is no failure signal to trigger on

decided.rule: cheapest candidate whose Wilson 95% lower bound >= best - 0.02, by cost per success; harness-lost runs excluded from the rate

fix_bug.what: fix a bug given a failing test; the agent reads, edits and can run the suite
fix_bug.why_no_escalation: with the runner every tier is 21/21; without it a bigger model fails the same way (partial fix, stops after one defect)
fix_bug.without_runner: no tier is reliable when there may be more than one defect: haiku 16/21, sonnet 14/21, fable 16/21
requires: the test runner in the loop (KUnit)

decided.rule: cheapest candidate whose Wilson 95% lower bound >= best - 0.02, by cost per success; harness-lost runs excluded from the rate

write_tests.what: write a test suite for a function; success = builds, passes on real code, fails on a seeded bug
write_tests.without_runner: do not use any tier: haiku 5/10, sonnet 7/10, fable 4/10, all with wrong expected values
requires: the test runner in the loop (KUnit)

decided.rule: cheapest candidate whose Wilson 95% lower bound >= best - 0.02, by cost per success; harness-lost runs excluded from the rate

browser_flow.what: drive a web page through a numbered checklist in a real Chrome tab (Claude-in-Chrome tools only, no source, no network/console); report pass/fail per item; measured on a toy app (cell 4) and on the author's own Go web store (cell 5)
browser_flow.why_no_escalation: haiku matched sonnet item for item on both apps; the misses were one lenient reading by fable, four over-strict readings by sonnet, and four browser disconnects in 76 store runs on all three tiers; no model missed a planted defect in a flow it finished
browser_flow.checker: a scripted user (bench/browser_flow/oracle.py) drives the same app and gives the truth vector; the app's action log confirms the flow was really driven

evidence.haiku low: 33/33 correct over 3 trials, full flow driven every time

not_measured: more than one trial for sonnet and fable on the toy app
browser_flow.retry_rule: re-run a flow whose request log shows it did not finish (grade.py drove != full): a browser disconnect, not a model miss; do not step up

evidence_own_app.what: the author's own Go web store at a pinned commit, 15 flows (14 planted defects plus clean), 10 items, truth from the fixture's scripted user, bench/own_app_flow/oracle.py, a local file (results/cell5)
evidence_own_app.haiku low: 30 correct of 32 runs (2 trials plus 2 reruns); both misses were the shared browser closed mid-flow, both flows rerun correct; 30/30 among finished flows
evidence_own_app.sonnet low: 26 correct of 31 runs; one browser cut (rerun correct), four extra fails on the item next to the defect; every planted defect flagged in every finished flow; 26/30 among finished flows
evidence_own_app.fable low: 15 correct of 16 runs: one trial 14/15 (the miss a browser cut) plus a rerun of that flow, correct; 15/15 among finished flows
evidence_own_app.browser_disconnects: 4 of 76 runs (haiku 2, sonnet 1, fable 1): the user closed the shared Chrome by mistake during the runs; each flow was rerun afterwards

decided.rule: cheapest candidate whose Wilson 95% lower bound >= best - 0.02, by cost per success; harness-lost runs excluded from the rate

unmeasured.what: everything else (review, design, writing, exploratory browser testing, visual review, ...)
unmeasured.why: no evidence; a cheap model's miss is silent where there is no checker (cell 1), so no blind downgrade

repo_fix.what: fix a bug with a failing test in a private repository of the author's (TypeScript, vitest); the transfer check for fix_bug on the user's own code
repo_fix.why_no_escalation: not needed with the runner: every Claude tier fixes 24/24 at every effort
requires: the test runner in the loop (vitest)

decided.rule: cheapest candidate whose Wilson 95% lower bound >= best - 0.02, by cost per success; harness-lost runs excluded from the rate

web_research.what: look up a technical fact on the web and cite a page that states it (answer pattern plus a fetch of every cited URL; 8 of 26 questions have a live truth fetched at grading time)
web_research.why_no_escalation: none: every tier finds the fact with a real source; the failure to watch is a right answer with no usable source

decided.rule: cheapest candidate whose Wilson 95% lower bound >= best - 0.02, by cost per success; harness-lost runs excluded from the rate

research_synthesis.what: write a short research note (250-700 words) that answers three looked-up questions, each claim with the page that states it; graded in code (answer patterns, every cited page fetched), prose quality beyond that not judged
research_synthesis.why_no_escalation: none: every tier above Haiku wrote every note with sources; Haiku missed the bar on citations, not on facts. The failure to watch is a right claim with a page that does not state it, the same as web_research.

evidence.haiku low: 16/18 over 3 trials (2 notes right but one claim cited a page that did not state it)

decided.rule: cheapest candidate whose Wilson 95% lower bound >= best - 0.02, by cost per success; harness-lost runs excluded from the rate

research_synthesis.note: first measurement 2026-11-02 (results/cell9): fact-dense notes graded in code; prose quality beyond the facts and sources is not judged. Sonnet low writes a sourced note at 1/5.7 of Fable low and 1/1.9 of Opus low.

rules: effort low first; medium bought nothing on the one family where it was swept
give the agent a checker (build, tests) before giving it a bigger model
no blind downgrade where there is no checker

the fixed prefix (~95k tokens, ~27k written per new session) is most of a short session's bill: count sessions on expensive models, not tokens; browser flows (40-50 tool calls) are the exception, there cache reads dominate and tokens per session matter too
user override wins: per-invocation model, then the agent file, then this file
a run the checker shows did not finish (browser disconnect, tool failure) gets a retry on the same tier, not a bigger model

engineering-minimal-change-engineer.md.note: has Bash, so the test runner is in the loop; run the tests before finishing
engineering-minimal-change-engineer.md.instruction: Before you finish a fix, run the tests that cover it (the failing test and its suite) and read the result. If anything still fails, keep going: there may be more than one defect. Report the test command and its outcome with your diff.

testing-api-tester.md.note: has Bash, so the test runner is in the loop
testing-api-tester.md.instruction: Run every test you write before you finish, and fix the test or the expectation until it passes on the current code. A test you did not run is not a deliverable.

testing-evidence-collector.md.note: closest agent to the measured family; its screenshot/visual-review and 'minimum 3-5 issues' parts are not measured
testing-evidence-collector.md.instruction: When you are given a page and a checklist, drive every step in order in the browser, judge each item only by what you actually see on screen, and report pass or fail per item with one sentence of evidence for each fail. Do not report a failure you did not observe. If the browser disconnects or a step cannot be run, mark those items not_run and say where the flow stopped, so the caller can retry.

web-researcher.md.note: a new agent file (2026-11-01): the research calls in the transcripts went to the built-in general-purpose agent, which no file can route; this file is the way to route them
web-researcher.md.instruction: Answer from pages you read in this session, not from memory. Give the answer first, then the URL of every page you actually opened that states it; never cite a page you did not open. If no page states it, say so.

recheck_when: catalog/discover.py reports a new or delisted model id
a routed family's success rate drops in use
